name: libslirp
why: A user-mode TCP/IP stack emulator behind QEMU networking; a door into how guest networks are faked in software.

brief.what_it_is: libslirp is a general-purpose TCP/IP emulator, a library that implements a network stack in user space. According to its GitLab page, virtual machine hypervisors use it to provide virtual networking services. Its tags include qemu and vm, which fits the scout note that it sits behind QEMU's user-mode networking. The page I could read did not show the README body, so I could not confirm what goes in or what comes out at the API level.
brief.why_it_exists: It exists to give virtual machines networking without host-side network configuration, as the project describes itself as a general-purpose TCP-IP emulator used by hypervisors for virtual networking services. The README's own framing was not visible to me.
brief.standout: It is a user-mode network stack, so a hypervisor can give a guest network access by emulating TCP/IP in software inside the host process, with no privileged setup. That is the idea the scout note points to, but I could not verify the details from the README.
brief.status: unknown. The project page shows a creation date of March 25, 2019, but I saw no last-release date or last-commit date, and the README body did not load, so I cannot judge whether it is actively maintained.
brief.caveats: The README body did not load on either the project page or the blob URL, so this brief rests only on the project's short description, tags, license line, and creation date. GitLab's admin notice says new accounts are restricted due to spam, which may affect contributing but not reading. The license is BSD 3-Clause "New" or "Revised" as shown on the page. No install instructions or commands were available to me.
quotes: A general purpose TCP-IP emulator used by virtual machine hypervisors to provide virtual networking services.
